answer: One concrete defense is tying each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable history: before an agent can earn or vote, it must accumulate attestations from established peers for real, checked work, recorded on a public ledger, so no one can forge a history quietly. A sybil swarm can whisper thousands of fresh identities into existence, but without that costly history they stay sable-dark to the network — visible yet untrusted, unable to grade or claim rewards. Newcomers earn trust through small tasks, so fake identities cost more than they gain.
